"heading": "C — Vehicle equipment", "learner_facing": true, "markdown": "## C — Vehicle equipment
Domain: required vehicle equipment and driver-assist limits, printed pages 90-92 [A01].
Pedagogic emphasis: lamp colors and visibility distances carry the most testable detail [A02].

FACT_ID: sec15-F01 | anchor: A01
Driver-assist features only aid the driver and never assume responsibility for operating the vehicle [A01].
Why it matters: frames every ADAS limit as driver responsibility.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F02 | anchor: A01
Parking assist and cruise control aids must not be used during the driving skills test [A01].
Why it matters: test-day ban to memorize.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F03 | anchor: A01
Drivers must stay engaged, consult the owner manual, know system limits, and keep sensors clean and software current [A01].
Why it matters: groups the care duties into one checklist.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F04 | anchor: A01
Every motor vehicle needs compliant brakes on all wheels, except a truck or truck tractor with three or more axles may omit front-wheel brakes [A01].
Why it matters: exception is the likely trap.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F05 | anchor: A01
With anti-lock brakes on a slick surface, hold steady firm pressure instead of pumping the pedal [A01].
Why it matters: corrects the old pumping habit.
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0100]

FACT_ID: sec15-F06 | anchor: A02
A bus, RV, or trailer at least 80 inches wide needs two amber front clearance lamps plus side lamps and two red rear lamps, all seen from 500 feet at night [A02].
Why it matters: combines width trigger, color, count and distance.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F07 | anchor: A02
A load reaching four feet or more past the bed or body needs two rear flags by day at least 12 inches square, or lamps seen from 500 feet at night [A02].
Why it matters: day versus night marking contrast.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F08 | anchor: A02
Trucks, truck tractors, and buses carry three flares or red emergency reflectors or lights plus two red flags, seen and distinguished from 600 feet, with flares burning for 12 hours [A02].
Why it matters: vehicle set plus distance plus burn time.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F09 | anchor: A02
Except motorcycles, each vehicle needs two white headlights reaching 350 feet on high beam and 100 feet on low beam, plus a high-beam indicator [A02].
Why it matters: pairs the two distances with the indicator.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F10 | anchor: A02
Every motor vehicle needs a working horn heard from 200 feet, and every vehicle needs a white plate lamp making the plate readable from 50 feet [A02].
Why it matters: two short distances tested together.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F11 | anchor: A02
Mud flaps or guards are required on vehicles rated 10,500 pounds or more, altered-suspension or altered-tire vehicles, and trailers unladen at 750 pounds or more [A02].
Why it matters: three triggers share one rule.
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0101]

FACT_ID: sec15-F12 | anchor: A03
Red or blue light seen from the front is reserved for emergency, school, snow-removal, or otherwise authorized vehicles [A03].
Why it matters: front-color prohibition with authorized exceptions.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F13 | anchor: A03
Each vehicle needs an amber side reflector near the front and a red one near the rear, seen from 500 feet at night and mounted 15 to 60 inches high [A03].
Why it matters: color, position, distance and height in one check.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F14 | anchor: A03
Vehicles need two red rear tail and stop lamps seen from 500 feet in daylight, and turn signals seen from 100 feet in normal sunlight [A03].
Why it matters: daylight distances for rear lamps versus signals.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

FACT_ID: sec15-F15 | anchor: A03
All windshield vehicles need at least one working wiper, both wipers when factory-fitted with two, and multi-speed wipers on models built after 1967 [A03].
Why it matters: wiper count and model-year rule.
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ut-class-d:utah-dld:handbook:pdf-0102]

Misconceptions: assist systems drive alone; ABS needs pumping; any front red or blue lamp is allowed.
Mnemonics: far lights far numbers for headlamp and flare distances.
Glossary: clearance lamp means wide-vehicle marker [A02]; reflector means passive side marker [A03]; ADAS means driver-assist safety system [A01].
